text: You again. Still staring at the front?
heard: You again, still staring at the front.

text: Colour is not my trade. Ask me about wood.
heard: Color is not my trade. Ask me about wood.

text: Smiths, carpenters, all the trades have their work yards inside this fort.
heard: Smiths, carpenters, all the trades have their work yards inside this fort.

text: Want a picture of it? Find someone with time. I have none.

text: Careful at the edge. It is a long way down.
heard: Careful at the edge. It is a long way down.

text: Two gates into this fort. The Delhi Gate to the north, the Mysore Gate to the south.
heard: Two gates into this fort, the Delhi gate to the north, the Mysore gate to the south.

text: Look at the ditch. Deep and wide, and dry in most parts.
heard: Look at the ditch, deep and wide, and dry in most parts.

text: This wall looks like stone all the way through. Inside, it is red clay.
heard: This wall looks like stone all the way through, inside it is red clay.

text: Go on down. The palace is the pretty part.
heard: Go on down. The palace is the pretty part.

text: Mind the bags. They are heavier than they look.
heard: Mind the bags, they are heavier than they look.

text: The granaries are inside the fort, behind their own wall.
heard: The granaries are inside the fort behind their own wall.

text: On a darbar day, we are allowed into the open court.
heard: On a Darbar day, we are allowed into the open court.

text: The court has fountains, to cool the air.
heard: The court has fountains to cool the air.

text: Now look up. Everyone does.
heard: Now look up, everyone does.

text: Please step around. We have only just set it down.
heard: Please step around. We have only just set it down.

text: My shoulders know every road in this fort.
heard: My shoulders know every road in this fort.

text: The highest officers get a balcony, at each end of the court.
heard: The highest officers get a balcony at each end of the court.

text: The lower officers have the hall under the ruler's balcony.
heard: The lower officers have the hall under the ruler's balcony.

text: Us? We wait out here with everybody else.

text: Going up? Mind your head.
heard: Going up, mind your head.

text: See these columns? They rise as high as the roof of the upper storey.
heard: See these columns, they rise as high as the roof of the upper story.

text: On a durbar day, nobody like us goes up there.

text: But you are not from here. Go on.

text: Not there, please. That pile is in order.

text: The principal departments of the government sit in this palace now.
heard: The principal departments of the government sit in this palace now.

text: A palace is a strange place to keep ledgers.

text: Somebody has mixed up these dated papers. Put them in order for me, will you?
